summary_sentence: For example, Sydney sits 1,160.0 km south of the Tropic of Capricorn, while Brisbane is just inside the tropics' edge — Australia straddles the line the way the US nearly touches the other one.
quick_answer: The Distance From Tropic of Capricorn Calculator measures the shortest surface distance from your point to the Tropic of Capricorn at 23.4367 degrees south — the southernmost latitude the Sun can reach overhead. Enter a place and read your distance from the southern fence.

body.t: The line crosses Australia, Namibia, Brazil and Chile — roadside markers included. Know your distance before the drive.

Inside the line the Sun tops the sky (December solstice on the line itself); outside, never. Your side of the fence is a solar fact for life.
The world's great deserts cluster near the tropics' edges — distance to Capricorn is a first clue in that pattern for southern continents.

Sydney (−33.87°): 1,160.0 km south of the line. Brisbane (−27.47°): ~448 km south — still outside. The line crosses Queensland far to the north, near Rockhampton, which markets itself on exactly this fact.
São Paulo (−23.55°) sits ~13 km inside the tropics — the line grazes the city's south. A megacity can straddle a great circle of latitude.

faq: The Sun stood in Capricornus at the December solstice when the ancients named it; precession has moved the solstice Sun into Sagittarius since. The geography kept the name.
When is the Sun overhead on this line?
At the December solstice's local noon — the southern summer's peak, and the mirror of Cancer's June moment.
Inside or outside the line — does it say?
Yes: the result's framing tells you which side of the line your point sits on (for circles and tropics, poleward versus equatorward; for the meridian, east versus west).
The shortest surface distance to the line — for latitude lines that is the meridian arc; for the prime meridian it is the great-circle route to the nearest point of the meridian.
Stand on the line and it is: the tropics and circles have real ground you can occupy, and the result honours it.
Sphere-accurate to well under a kilometre for these magnitudes — plenty for education, planning and curiosity; geodesists refine with the ellipsoid.
Signs and hemispheres are handled — a southern point measures to southern lines by the same geometry.
